web_search_deadline_s.note: Deadline for one web_search call, search plus page fetches; smaller than the 120 s request deadline (RA-11).

run_python_deadline_margin_s.note: Extra time beyond the call's timeout_s for sandbox restore and result upload, so the executor deadline = timeout_s + this margin.

tool_calls_per_user_per_minute.note: Per-user token bucket for tool calls (step 5 of the loop); separate from the request rate limit of Part 03.

max_parallel_calls_per_pass.note: Most tool calls of one pass that the orchestrator runs at the same time; more calls wait for a free slot.

approval_wait_s.note: How long a side-effecting call waits for the user's approval before it returns a 'not approved' tool result.

broker_token_ttl_s.note: Lifetime of the access token the credential broker hands to an executor for one call (RA-31).

web_search_provider._about: The external search provider of Option A (RA-28), as seen from the orchestrator in ap_south.

per_query_latency_p50_ms.note: Median time from request sent to full JSON response for one query, including the network path to the provider. Public search APIs do not publish latency; a few hundred ms is a realistic order.

per_query_latency_p95_ms.note: 95th percentile per query. With p50 it fixes a lognormal latency model in sim/web_search_budget.py.

request_timeout_ms.note: Per-attempt timeout on one provider call; about 2x p95, so a timeout means a real fault, not a slow tail.

results_per_query.note: count requested per query. Public APIs allow up to 20 (Brave, Tavily); 5 keeps the tool result small. For the reference request 3 x 5 = 15 raw results dedupe to 8 unique.

price_usd_per_1000_queries.note: Contract price of the hypothetical provider. The public anchor is one vendor's list price of 10 USD per 1,000 searches for its own tool (retrieval_and_data.anthropic_web_search_price_per_1000).

contracted_qps_per_region.note: Quota agreed with the provider for each of the 4 serving regions. Above it the provider returns 429.

mean_queries_per_search.note: Fleet mean. The reference request uses 3.

mean_pages_fetched_per_search.note: Fleet mean of fetch_top actually fetched. The reference request fetches 3.

search_cache_hit_fraction.note: Share of normalized queries answered from the tenant-scoped search-result cache (RA-19) within their TTL.

web_search_pipeline._about: Orchestrator-side steps around the provider call.

cache_lookup_ms.note: One Redis GET per normalized query inside the region (RA-19); the 3 lookups run in parallel.

rerank_latency_ms.note: M-rerank scores the 8 unique snippets (about 80 tokens each) against the user's question in one small batch.

breaker_window_calls.note: Circuit breaker on the provider (RA-13): failure rate measured over the last 20 calls per orchestrator pod.

breaker_min_calls.note: The breaker does not open before 10 calls are in the window.

breaker_failure_rate_to_open.note: Open when at least half of the calls in the window failed or timed out.

breaker_open_duration_s.note: Time in the open state before half-open trials.

breaker_half_open_trials.note: Trial calls allowed in half-open; all 3 must succeed to close.

web_fetch._about: Limits and latencies of the egress service that fetches pages (RA-29), running in ap_south.

allowed_schemes.note: Protocol allowlist; file, ftp, gopher, data and all others are rejected before DNS.

allowed_ports.note: Only the default web ports; blocks probes of internal services on other ports.

max_redirects.note: Each hop is parsed and checked again; the sixth redirect fails the fetch.

connect_timeout_ms.note: TCP plus TLS handshake limit per connection.

total_timeout_ms.note: Wall-clock limit for one page, from DNS to the last body byte, redirects included.

max_response_bytes.note: Body limit after decompression; the fetcher stops reading at this size and keeps what it has.

allowed_content_types.note: Media types passed to text extraction. PDF and images are out of scope for this tool in this reference system.

dns_resolve_ms.note: Recursive resolution through the egress service's own resolver, cache miss.

origin_rtt_ms.note: Round trip from the egress service in ap_south to the CDN edge in front of a typical vendor website.

server_time_p50_ms.note: Origin time to first byte after the request, median.

server_time_p95_ms.note: Origin time to first byte, 95th percentile (dynamic pricing pages are often slow).

page_html_bytes_reference.note: Mean HTML size of one pricing page (markup, inline scripts and styles; no sub-resources fetched).

download_mbps.note: Effective per-connection download rate after TCP slow start for a page of this size.

extract_ms_per_page.note: CPU time to parse HTML, drop boilerplate and hidden elements, and keep the main text.

web_cache_ttl._about: TTLs of the search-result and page-text caches per query class (RA-19). The orchestrator assigns the class from the query and the recency_days argument.

reference_docs_s.note: Static documentation, standards, encyclopedic pages: change rarely.

general_s.note: Default class for queries with no time words.

product_pricing_s.note: Prices and plans: change without notice, and a stale price gives a wrong number in an answer.

weather_s.note: Forecasts update a few times per hour at most.

stock_quote_s.note: Not cached; quotes come from a market-data API, not from web search.

empty_result_s.note: Negative cache for queries with zero results, so a burst of the same failing query does not hit the provider.

fetched_page_default_s.note: Page text when the origin sends no Cache-Control or Expires; never longer than the query class TTL.

own_index_sizing._about: Illustrative inputs for the Option B sizing arithmetic (7.3). Not a claim about any real search engine.

indexed_pages.note: A large general web index for illustration.

mean_recrawl_interval_days.note: Average over all pages; news pages recrawl in minutes, archives in months.

raw_html_bytes_per_page.note: HTML only, compressed transfer not counted.

postings_bytes_per_token.note: Positional postings with delta and variable-byte coding; a few bytes per posting is the textbook order.

passages_per_page.note: Embedded passages per page for dense retrieval.

render_fraction.note: Pages whose main text needs JavaScript, so a headless browser renders them.

render_cpu_s.note: Headless browser with sub-resource fetches and script execution. Estimate; no public ratio exists.

web_story._about: Part 07 additions to the reference story. Competitor names, queries, recency_days and current prices are hypothetical.tool_call_story (Part 06).

birchline_previous_eur_per_seat_month.note: Birchline's price before its August 2026 increase; a stale comparison page still shows it (7.7).

sandbox_vm._about: Size and limits of one code sandbox: one Firecracker microVM per session (RA-30). Part 08.1.

vcpus.note: Guest vCPU count (Firecracker machine config); the host cgroup cpu.max caps the VM at the same number of host CPUs.

memory_mib.note: Guest memory; enough for pandas, numpy and matplotlib on report-sized data. The host reserves it in full (no memory overcommit).

scratch_disk_mib.note: Writable, sparse per-session block device for /tmp and the home directory; deleted with the session.

output_quota_mib.note: Most bytes the guest agent copies out of /mnt/output per call; files beyond it are not returned.

artifact_max_files.note: Most files returned from /mnt/output per call.

pids_max.note: Guest cgroup pids.max for the code's process tree; fork() then fails with EAGAIN (stops fork bombs).

idle_keep_live_s.note: After a call ends, the session VM stays running this long for the next call of the same session, so Python variables survive; then the host stops the VM and keeps only the session's files.

session_retention_s.note: How long the session's files (scratch disk and /mnt/output) are kept in the object store for later turns; a later call gets a fresh VM with the files copied back in, but no Python state. Then the files are deleted.

artifact_url_ttl_s.note: Lifetime of the presigned GET URL the file API issues for one artifact download (RA-63).

sandbox_pool._about: Start-up times, session shape and host size used for warm-pool sizing (Part 08.1). Firecracker publishes boot time but no snapshot-restore time, so restore values are hypothetical.

vmm_start_ms.note: Wall time from process start to API socket; the Firecracker specification gives a typical 12 ms (range 6 to 60 ms).

guest_agent_ready_ms.note: Cold path: from guest /sbin/init to the guest agent listening on vsock (mounts, user setup, agent start).

python_warm_imports_ms.note: Cold path: start the Python interpreter and import numpy, pandas and matplotlib. The pool snapshot is taken after this step.

snapshot_restore_ms.note: Load the template snapshot into a new jailed Firecracker process, resume it and complete the vsock handshake (memory pages load later, on demand).

pool_warmup_ms.note: After restore, the agent reseeds user-space random state and runs a tiny warm-up script that faults in the interpreter's pages, before the VM joins the pool.

pool_claim_ms.note: Sandbox manager takes a ready VM from the host's pool and binds it to the session.

copy_in_ms.note: Guest agent receives the session's uploaded files (the 2.1 MB Q3 report) over vsock into /mnt/data.

reference_run_ms.note: Run time of the reference request's 16-line margin script, mostly matplotlib rendering and savefig.

artifact_upload_ms.note: Copy the PNG out over vsock, scan its type and size, and PUT it to the object store.

mean_run_s.note: Mean run time of one code call across the fleet (most calls are short data and chart scripts).

calls_per_session.note: Mean code calls in one sandbox session (one conversation's code work).

mean_gap_between_calls_s.note: Mean time between two calls of the same session (one more inference pass, or the user's next turn); shorter than idle_keep_live_s, so the VM is still live.

burst_safety_z.note: Pool headroom above the Little's Law mean: arrivals in the refill window are treated as Poisson, so the pool adds z × sqrt(mean).

host_vcpus.note: Hardware threads of one sandbox host (two 48-core CPUs with SMT).

host_reserved_gib.note: Host memory kept for the host kernel, page cache of snapshot files, jailer and Firecracker overhead.

computer_use._about: The browser tool's observe-act loop for a 20-step task (Part 08.2). Not part of the reference request.

viewport_width_px.note: Width of the remote browser's viewport and of each screenshot.

viewport_height_px.note: Height of the remote browser's viewport and of each screenshot.

steps_per_task.note: Screenshot-action steps for one browser task, for example filling a multi-page web form.

task_text_tokens.note: The user's task description in the context.

tool_schema_tokens.note: The browser tool's schema (actions, coordinates, keys) in the tool-declare message.

action_tokens_per_step.note: The tool call of one action, for example a click with x, y coordinates.

result_frame_tokens.note: Text tokens of the tool-result message around each screenshot (frame, step number, URL).

kept_screenshots.note: Option B: only the last 3 screenshots stay in the context; older ones become a short text placeholder.

placeholder_tokens.note: Text that replaces a removed screenshot in option B.

capture_ms.note: Capture the viewport, encode PNG and write it to the object store.

action_exec_ms.note: The browser VM runs one click or key action.

page_settle_ms.note: Wait after an action for navigation, network and rendering before the next screenshot.

routing_endpoints_ref._about: State of three M-frontier decode endpoints (attention-DP ranks of DEP16 decode workers) in ap_south at the moment pass 2 of the reference request reaches the endpoint picker. E1 decoded pass 1. Blocks are 64-token KV blocks (the K3 block size on GB300).

names.note: E1 served pass 1 of the reference request; E2 holds the tenant's stable prefix from another user of the same organization; E3 holds no block under this tenant's cache salt.

running_sequences.note: vllm:num_requests_running per endpoint; below the 74 sequences of 8k context that one rank's KV pool holds (kv_math).

waiting_requests.note: vllm:num_requests_waiting per endpoint at the last scrape.

in_flight_requests.note: Requests the EPP dispatched and has not seen finish; larger than waiting + running when the scrape lags the dispatches.

active_decode_blocks.note: KV blocks held by the running sequences (mean about 5,500 tokens of context per sequence).

active_prefill_tokens.note: Uncached prompt tokens dispatched to the endpoint and not yet prefilled (local prefill of short suffixes, RA-38). The EPP's in-flight token count uses the same number.

g1_overlap_blocks.note: Blocks of pass 2's prefix in each endpoint's HBM. E1: the 23,552 reusable tokens of pass 1 (context_budget p2.prefix_hit_tokens_512). E2: the tenant's stable prefix, 1,536 tokens (context_budget p1.stable_prefix_hit_512).

g2_overlap_blocks.note: Blocks in pinned host DRAM (G2) for the main case; the tier variant moves E1's blocks there.

g3_overlap_blocks.note: Blocks on local NVMe (G3) for the main case.

routing_endpoints_overloaded._about: Variant of routing_endpoints_ref in which E1 is overloaded: a burst of long prompts landed on it just before pass 2. E2 and E3 keep their values.

e1_active_prefill_tokens.note: About 2.5 s of prefill work at the calibrated 16,000 tokens/s.

routing_endpoints_burst._about: Second snapshot of E1-E3 a few seconds later during a regional burst, for the flow-control saturation example (RA-41).

running_sequences.note: Close to the 74-sequence limit of one rank at 8k.

in_flight_requests.note: Equal to waiting + running: the scrape is current.

active_decode_blocks.note: KV blocks of the running sequences.

peak_prefill_tokens_per_s.note: peakPrefillThroughput set on the prefix-cache-affinity-filter for one K3 decode endpoint's local prefill. llm-d's default 15,928 is calibrated for Qwen3-32B on 2x H100; a real deployment measures its own value with the calibration guide. Also the prefill rate of one endpoint in sim/routing_policies_sim.py.

routing_sim._about: Inputs of the seeded routing-policy simulation (sim/routing_policies_sim.py). One pool of identical endpoints; illustrative mixed chat workload, not a fleet measurement.

warmup_s.note: Requests that arrive before this time are left out of the statistics.

conversation_rate_per_s.note: Poisson arrival rate of new conversations.

mean_turns_per_conversation.note: Geometric number of turns per conversation.

mean_think_time_s.note: Exponential gap between a response and the next turn.

first_prompt_sigma.note: Gives prompts from tens of tokens to about 100k tokens.

followup_new_tokens_median.note: New user tokens in each later turn.

followup_new_tokens_sigma.note: Spread of the new user tokens per later turn.

prompt_min_tokens.note: Clip of the prompt distribution (spec R-IX.2 example).

prompt_max_tokens.note: Clip of the prompt distribution (spec R-IX.2 example).

output_min_tokens.note: Clip of the output distribution (spec R-IX.2 example).

output_max_tokens.note: Clip of the output distribution (spec R-IX.2 example).

kv_capacity_tokens.note: KV pool of one simulated endpoint; running contexts and cached prefixes share it (cached entries are evicted LRU).

tpot_base_ms.note: Decode step time with one sequence.

tpot_per_running_ms.note: Added step time per running sequence (more KV to read).

kv_block_tokens.note: Block size used by the Dynamo cost in the simulation.

hot_prefix_sim._about: Hot-prefix scenario of sim/routing_score.py: one large tenant sends many short requests that all start with the same long prefix (system prompt + tool schemas, hypothetical.serving_assumptions.reference_shared_prefix_tokens).

hot_fraction.note: Share of conversations that belong to the hot tenant.

hot_suffix_median_tokens.note: Median new suffix after the shared prefix (matches serving_assumptions.prefix_hit_suffix_tokens).

conversation_rate_per_s.note: Higher rate than routing_sim, because hot requests are short.

low_gate_ms.note: maxTTFTPenaltyMs of the 'load threshold' variant, instead of the default 18,000 ms.

admission_ref._about: Priority bands of the reference system's EPP flow control (InferenceObjective.spec.priority; higher = more critical).

band_names.note: Paid interactive chat, free-tier chat, and background jobs (evaluations, offline summaries).

band_priorities.note: Strict priority across bands; the reference request runs in 'interactive'.

reference_request_band.note: The reference user's plan is a paid plan.

batch_band_usage_ceiling.note: The batch band dispatches only while pool saturation is below 0.8, which keeps headroom for interactive bands.

retry_after_s.note: Retry-After the model router adds when it turns an EPP 429 into a client 429 (llm-d's 429 carries no Retry-After).

fairness_ref._about: Fairness inside one priority band: llm-d program-aware-fairness with the las strategy, keyed by tenant ID. The weights equal the plugin defaults.

las_output_token_weight.note: Output tokens count twice in attained service (strategy_las.go).

toy_tenants.note: Illustrative tenants of the fairness example.

toy_prompt_tokens.note: Prompt tokens each tenant consumed in its completed requests.

toy_head_wait_ms.note: Wait of each tenant's oldest queued request.

drr_queue_a_tokens.note: Tenant A: one long-document request, then a short one (backend.long_document_prompt_tokens).

drr_queue_b_tokens.note: Tenant B: four chat requests of the mean prompt size.

pool_queueing._about: Inputs for Little's Law at the ap_south M-frontier pool (Part 9.5). Part 14 owns fleet sizing.

ap_south_share_of_asia_pacific.note: Share of asia_pacific traffic that ap_south serves.

m_frontier_share_of_requests.note: Share of requests that select M-frontier.

extra_passes_per_tool_request.note: Mean extra inference passes of a request that uses tools; the reference request has 2.

mean_tool_time_s.note: Mean time of one tool call between passes.

gateway_queue_wait_s.note: Mean wait in the EPP flow-control queue at peak.

engine_wait_s.note: Mean time in the engine's waiting queue before the first prefill chunk.

prefill_time_s.note: Mean prefill time per pass, prefix hits included.

mmc_servers.note: Endpoints behind one shared queue in the M/M/c comparison.

decode_step_tokens_e1.note: Local prefill chunk in E1's step at the counter moment (in addition to one token per running sequence).

generation_guards._about: Part 10 (Transformer internals, §10.14) reference-system guards against generation failures. They use vLLM's public sampling parameters; real providers' settings are not public (class D).

repetition_max_pattern_tokens.note: vLLM RepetitionDetectionParams.max_pattern_size: the longest repeated token pattern the engine looks for. 64 tokens covers a repeated sentence or a repeated short list item.

repetition_min_pattern_tokens.note: min_pattern_size: patterns shorter than 8 tokens (for example '| ' table separators or digit runs) repeat legitimately, so they never stop a stream.

repetition_min_count.note: min_count: a pattern must repeat 6 times back to back before the engine stops the sequence with FINISHED_REPETITION. Low enough to stop a loop within a few hundred tokens, high enough to allow a 5-row table with identical rows.

malformed_output_regenerations.note: When the orchestrator rejects a tool call or a JSON answer that fails schema validation, it runs the pass once more with the validation error appended; a second failure returns an error to the client. Separate from the transport retry layer of RA-12.

gpu_step_model._about: Kernel efficiency assumptions of the roofline step-time model (sim/gpu_step_lib.py). Compute efficiency reuses hypothetical.serving_assumptions.prefill_mfu.

hbm_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Share of the datasheet HBM bandwidth that large streaming reads (weights, KV) reach in a well-tuned kernel. Assumption; a real deployment measures it.

per_layer_overhead_us.note: Time per decoder layer that neither FLOPs nor bytes explain: kernel tails and gaps between about 14 kernels, and the latency of the two tensor-parallel all-reduces (Part 12). Assumption.

per_step_overhead_ms.note: Per scheduler iteration: embedding lookup, sampling, copying token IDs to the CPU, graph replay launch. Assumption; async scheduling hides the CPU scheduler itself (RA-35).

batching_ref._about: Inputs of the Part 11 batching simulations (sim/continuous_batching_sim.py, sim/chunked_prefill_sim.py, sim/roofline.py).

roofline_batch_sizes.note: Batch sizes placed on the roofline (R-XI.4 asks for several).

decode_batch_example.note: The R-XI.8 example: 64 decode sequences, one new token each.

static_batch_size.note: Batch size of the static-batching baseline, equal to the R-XI.8 batch.

length_lognormal_sigma.note: Shape of the prompt and output length distributions; means come from hypothetical.traffic.

comparison_arrival_rate_rps.note: Poisson arrival rate of the static-versus-continuous comparison; chosen below the static baseline's saturation so that both policies keep up.

load_sweep_rates_rps.note: Poisson arrival rates of the utilization-versus-goodput sweep (R-XI.12), from light load to overload of one M-dense replica.

token_budget_example_decodes.note: R-XI.6 example: A and B each decode 1 token.

token_budget_example_prefills.note: R-XI.6 example: C and D prefill 4,000 and 4,190 tokens; with A and B the step holds exactly 8,192 tokens.

long_prompt_tokens.note: R-XI.7 example: one 100,000-token prompt with no prefix-cache hit.

long_prompt_running_decodes.note: Decodes already running on the replica when the long prompt arrives (the R-XI.8 batch).

chunk_budgets.note: Token budgets compared in the chunked-prefill sweep; 8,192 is the RA-36 default.

spec_acceptance_rate.note: Per-token acceptance rate used for M-draft (EAGLE) in the batch-size study; no acceptance figure for M-draft is published (research/notes/01-models.md §2.1.3).

tp_comm_ref._about: Inputs of the alpha-beta collective time model t = steps x alpha + bytes on the busiest link / (rated per-direction bandwidth x efficiency). NVIDIA publishes no NVLink or InfiniBand end-to-end latency (note 02 §2.4), so the per-step latencies are assumptions.

nvlink_step_latency_us.note: Kernel-side flag signalling plus one NVLink hop inside one HGX node. Assumption of the order that small-message microbenchmarks report; not a vendor value.

network_step_latency_us.note: One RDMA message GPU -> PCIe -> NIC -> leaf switch -> NIC -> PCIe -> GPU plus completion signalling. Assumption; NVIDIA gives no end-to-end figure.

nvlink_busbw_efficiency.note: Achieved bus bandwidth of a large AllReduce over NVLink 4. Assumption; measure with nccl-tests on the real node.

network_busbw_efficiency.note: Achieved bus bandwidth of a large AllReduce over one 400 Gb/s RDMA NIC per GPU. Assumption.

decode_batch_sequences.note: Example M-dense decode batch on H-teach, well below max_num_seqs (RA-36) and the KV limit of 8k-token sequences (part 13.1).

moe_routing_ref._about: Expert-load simulation for M-frontier under DEP16. No public per-expert load data exists for Kimi K3.

expert_popularity_zipf_exponent.unit: exponent s in p(rank r) proportional to r^-s
expert_popularity_zipf_exponent.note: Mild skew: the hottest of 896 experts gets about 5x the mean routing probability. Assumption to show hot experts; real skew depends on the traffic mix.

redundant_experts.unit: extra expert copies per DEP16 worker
redundant_experts.note: One redundant copy of a hot expert per GPU (896 + 16 = 912 slots, 57 per GPU), in the style of vLLM EPLB num_redundant_experts. Assumption.

decode_tokens_per_rank.unit: tokens per rank per decode step
decode_tokens_per_rank.note: TensorRT-LLM DEP16 concurrency 256 over 16 ranks (SRC-389); one token per sequence per step, no speculation.

fleet_price_ref._about: Illustrative GPU-hour prices for the price-per-performance formula (R-XII.9). Not market quotes and not any provider's cost.

gb300_gpu_hour_usd.note: Assumption for the formula only; includes the rack-scale NVLink domain.

fleet_scenarios._about: Scale scenarios for the population funnel (R-XIV.1). Every other ratio (requests per user, peak-to-average, connected share, output length, decode speed) stays at hypothetical.traffic.

daily_active_users.note: A small product, a mid-size product, the reference system (equals hypothetical.traffic.daily_active_users) and four times the reference.

capacity_targets._about: Planning targets and facility values for fleet sizing (R-XIV.2, R-XIV.3, R-XIV.6).

prefill_utilization_target.note: Prefill time adds directly to TTFT, and queue wait grows as 1/(1 − ρ) (part 9.5), so prefill pools run well below saturation.

decode_kv_fill_target.note: Decode workers are planned to hold 85% of the sequences their KV pool fits; the rest absorbs length variance without preemption (part 13.8).

h100_nodes_per_rack.note: Air-cooled H-teach racks with four 8-GPU nodes (about 41 kW at the DGX H100 maximum system power).

gb300_rack_power_kw.note: NVIDIA publishes no rack power for GB300 NVL72. HPE gives 132 kW nominal for GB200 NVL72 (SRC-033); OEM listings for GB300 range from about 132 to 142 kW. 140 kW is a planning value, not a datasheet figure.

headroom_over_peak.note: Capacity above the forecast regional peak for forecast error and bursts shorter than the autoscaler reaction time (RA-42).

request_cost_cases._about: The three text-only requests of R-XIV.4 (the fourth is the reference request). Values copied from the spec; all three run on M-frontier with no prefix-cache hit.

prompt_tokens.note: R-XIV.4 cases 1 to 3: short chat, long document, long generation.

workload_profiles._about: The three planning workloads of R-XIV.6 on M-frontier: A short support chat, B long PDF reasoning (prompt and output from hypothetical.backend.long_document_*), C an agent that runs several web searches.

a_prompt_tokens.note: System prompt (1,200, hypothetical.tool_loop) + a short history + the customer's question.

a_output_tokens.note: A short support answer, no reasoning.

a_prefix_hit_fraction.note: The 1,200-token system prompt hits the tenant's prefix cache (RA-40).

a_ttft_target_s.note: Support chat is interactive and short, so the first token must come fast.

b_prefix_hit_fraction.note: Mean over a session: the first question pays the whole document, follow-ups reuse it.

b_ttft_target_s.note: Users accept a longer wait for a long document; a progress event shows during prefill.

c_passes.note: Five tool passes (search, fetch, search, fetch, check) and one final answer; below max_tool_iterations 8.

c_first_prompt_tokens.note: System prompt, tool schemas, history and the task.

c_tokens_added_per_pass.note: Search snippets or fetched page text plus the previous pass's output, under fetched_page_tokens_cap.

c_ttft_target_s.note: Each pass sits on the critical path of a long task; status events show progress.

planning_rate_rps.note: The same arrival rate for all three workloads, to show that one requests/s number does not size a fleet.

region_demand._about: Per-region demand for the daily curve (R-XIV.8) over the four regions of RA-05. Shares combine hypothetical.traffic.regional_split, pool_queueing.ap_south_share_of_asia_pacific and the rest-of-world assignment below.

home_split_of_continent.note: Asia-Pacific split from pool_queueing.ap_south_share_of_asia_pacific. Rest of world: Latin America to us_east, west and north Africa to eu_west, east Africa, the Middle East and South Asia to ap_south (the Nairobi user is in this group).

utc_offset_hours.note: Local time of each region's users on 2026-10-09 (daylight time in Virginia and Dublin).

local_peak_hour.note: Work and study use dominates; the curve is lowest 12 hours later, at 03:00 local.

regional_peak_to_trough.note: Each region's busiest quarter hour over its quietest one. a flatter curve (was about 29×, solved from the global peak-to-average); real regions keep a floor of overnight use, API and agent work, and users who are awake at that local hour somewhere else.

shape.note: A von Mises daily shape with mean 1; the concentration κ follows from regional_peak_to_trough: κ = ln(peak-to-trough) / 2. The global peak-to-average then follows from the four offset regions (about 1.24); the planning peak hypothetical.traffic.peak_arrival_rate keeps a margin above that curve for the busiest weekday and event surges.

failover_partner.note: Next-nearest healthy region that receives a failed region's M-frontier traffic before any smaller model (RA-57).

background_work._about: Daily preemptible work that fills the troughs (R-XIV.8), as a fraction of the interactive GPU-hours of the same day. It runs in the 'batch' admission band (hypothetical.admission_ref).

batch_api_fraction.note: Batch API and flex-tier requests with a 24-hour completion window.

embedding_backfill_fraction.note: Re-embedding of workspace documents after an M-embed upgrade, and ingestion backlogs (runs on the retrieval pool's share).

offline_eval_fraction.note: Regression and quality evaluations of new model and prompt versions.

outage_s.note: The region's API is unreachable for one minute; clients that tried to send wait to retry.

retry_window_s.note: Full-jitter clients spread their first retry uniformly over [0, 30 s] after recovery (cap of the RA-12 backoff).

seed.note: RNG seed of the jittered retry draw.

capacity_over_mean.note: Admitted capacity of the region over its mean arrival rate at that hour: the 15% headroom plus warm spares.

news_search_fraction.note: During a breaking event, half of all requests trigger web search (normal: hypothetical.traffic.web_search_fraction).

news_query_cache_hit_fraction.note: Most users ask about the same event, so normalized queries repeat inside the search-result TTL (RA-19).

streaming_ref._about: Part 15 (Streaming back to pixels) reference-system values for the token stream from the model server to the browser (RA-47 to RA-50). What real providers use is not public (class D).

event_types.note: The client-facing event vocabulary of this reference system (RA-47: explicit event types). Illustrative; not the format of any real provider.

per_hop_stream_buffer_bytes.unit: bytes per stream per proxy hop
per_hop_stream_buffer_bytes.note: RA-49 bound on the application buffer that each proxy hop keeps for one response stream. At 100 tokens/s one client event is about 50 bytes, so 16 KiB holds a few seconds of stream; a larger buffer only hides a stalled client longer.

slow_client_stall_limit_s.note: When a stream's buffer stays full (the client reads nothing) for this long, the edge resets the stream; the cancellation travels down (RA-49) and the message is stored as interrupted (RA-59). Longer than a normal mobile handoff, far shorter than the 120 s top-level deadline.

in_region_hop_forward_ms.note: Time one in-region proxy or service hop adds to forward one small stream event (parse a frame, run filters, write a frame), plus the in-zone network. Assumption; a real deployment measures it from traces (RA-52).

display_refresh_hz.note: Refresh rate of the reference user's laptop display. Many phones and laptops run at 90-120 Hz; 60 Hz is the common lower case.

quic_dcid_bytes.note: Length of the destination connection ID that the edge chooses for its QUIC connections (RFC 9000 allows 0-20 bytes). 8 bytes leaves room for a server ID that the L4 balancer reads (RA-01).

quic_packet_number_bytes.note: Encoded packet number length in 1-RTT packets (RFC 9000 allows 1-4 bytes); 2 bytes covers the packets in flight on one connection.

quic_request_stream_id.note: The HTTP/3 request stream of your request on the warm connection: client-initiated bidirectional streams use IDs 0, 4, 8, ..., so 44 is the 12th request on this connection (page loads, uploads and earlier turns).

storage_ref._about: Sizing inputs for the conversation store (RA-17, RA-18). Part 16.1.

messages_per_request.note: One user message and one assistant message per turn (RA-18; part 3.5). Tool results stay inside the assistant message record.

mean_user_message_tokens.note: Mean new user text per turn; the rest of hypothetical.traffic.mean_prompt_tokens is system prompt, tools and history.

bytes_per_token_text.note: Mean UTF-8 bytes per token for mostly English text with a BPE vocabulary; a round estimate, not a measurement.

message_row_overhead_bytes.note: IDs (tenant, conversation, message), sequence number, timestamps, status, model ID, token counts, citation and file references, row header.

replicas_per_range.note: One voting replica per availability zone of the home region, the smallest group with a quorum (RA-17).

in_region_commit_ms.note: One quorum commit across availability zones of one region: about one inter-zone round trip plus a log flush. Assumption, not a vendor figure.

large_tenant_requests_per_s.note: Peak request rate of the largest single tenant (an enterprise organization) in the hot-row example.

quota_counter_shards.note: A hard-quota counter split into this many rows; the request picks one row at random and the check sums all of them.

tool_calls_per_tool_request.note: Mean tool calls of a request that uses tools; each call adds one inference pass. The reference request has 2 (web_search, run_python).

usage_event_bytes.note: Serialized Protobuf: event ID, tenant, user, request, pass number, model, region, token counts, timestamps. No text.

audit_event_bytes.note: Actor, action, resource IDs, decision, policy version, trace ID. No user text (part 18.4).

analytics_event_bytes.note: One request summary: stage timings, model, cache hits, sizes, status. No user text.

turn_completed_event_bytes.note: IDs only (tenant, user, conversation, message); consumers read the text from the conversation store.

min_insync_replicas.note: RA-20: with replication factor 3 and acks=all, a write needs 2 in-sync replicas, so one broker can fail without blocking producers.

usage_topic_partitions.note: Chosen above the consumer count the peak needs, so the billing aggregator can grow without a repartition.

aggregator_events_per_s.note: Events one billing-aggregator consumer process decodes, deduplicates and sums per second. Assumption.

dedupe_window_s.note: How long the aggregator remembers an event ID; longer than any producer retry or consumer replay of a normal day.

dedupe_entry_bytes.note: 16-byte event ID plus hash-table and TTL overhead in the dedupe store.

cache_map_ref._about: Lifetimes of the caches on the cache map that earlier parts left open (RA-19). Part 16.3.

static_asset_max_age_s.note: Cache-Control max-age for JS, CSS and font files whose names contain a content hash (one year), sent with immutable (RFC 8246).

app_shell_max_age_s.note: The HTML page that names the hashed files is sent with no-cache: every load revalidates it, so a new release reaches users at once.

entitlement_cache_ttl_s.note: Plan and entitlements per tenant in the Redis-compatible cache (part 3.1); a plan change reaches every gateway within one minute.

signing_key_cache_ttl_s.note: Public token-signing keys held in gateway process memory; a key rotation publishes the new key before it signs anything.

retrieval_result_ttl_s.note: Hybrid-retrieval result lists per tenant, ACL scope, index version and normalized query text; a document change bumps the index version.

billing_ref._about: Illustrative list prices and aggregation settings for usage billing (Part 16.4). Not any provider's prices.

price_cached_input_usd_per_mtok.note: Illustrative: a 90% discount for prompt tokens the prefix cache served.

price_output_usd_per_mtok.note: Illustrative; reasoning tokens are output tokens and pay this price (RA-60).

price_web_search_usd_per_1000_queries.note: Illustrative; billed per query sent to the search provider, not per tool call.

price_code_exec_usd_per_s.note: Illustrative; billed per second of run time of the run_python call (0.36 USD per hour).

price_storage_usd_per_gb_month.note: Illustrative; uploaded files in the object store, prorated by the day.

aggregation_window_s.note: The billing aggregator sums usage per tenant, model and usage kind over one hour before it writes a ledger row.

active_hours_per_tenant_per_day.unit: hours with usage per tenant per day
active_hours_per_tenant_per_day.note: Mean number of distinct hours in which one active tenant sends requests. Most tenants are single users.

timeout_budget_ref._about: Part 17.1 deadline split of the reference request (RA-11). The top-level deadline is hypothetical.slo.top_level_deadline_s; tool deadlines come from hypothetical.tool_exec_limits and Part 07/08 values. What real providers use is not public (class D).

edge_reserve_s.note: Time the edge PoP keeps after the gateway deadline to send an error event and close the stream cleanly; the gateway deadline is the edge deadline minus this.

gateway_reserve_s.note: Time the API gateway keeps after the orchestrator deadline to map an error to an HTTP status and log it.

final_write_reserve_s.note: Time the orchestrator keeps at the end for the final (or partial) message write (RA-18, RA-59) and the usage events; no child call may use it.

conversation_read_cap_s.note: Cap on the history read from the conversation store; about 100 times its normal time, so it fires only on a real fault (17.5).

memory_read_cap_s.note: Cap on the memory-record lookup (part 5.5); the request continues without memory if it expires.

memory_read_expected_s.note: Normal time of the memory lookup (embedding cache hit plus a small vector search).

retrieval_cap_s.note: Cap on hybrid retrieval with reranking (part 5.3); the request continues without workspace chunks if it expires.

tool_pass_cap_s.note: Cap on one inference pass that ends in a tool call (passes 1 and 2): queue + prefill + up to about 600 output tokens at 20 tokens/s.

final_pass_cap_s.note: Cap on the final answer pass (pass 3): about 1,000 output tokens at 20 tokens/s plus queue and prefill.

cancellation_ref._about: Part 17.2 cancellation chain and fleet waste (RA-49, RA-59).

cancel_fraction.note: Share of requests that the user stops (Stop button) or abandons (closed tab, lost network) before message.done. Assumption; a real service measures it.

mean_remaining_fraction.note: Mean share of the answer that is still to be generated when a cancel happens (cancels spread evenly over the stream).

in_region_hops_to_engine.note: In-region hops the cancel crosses after it reaches the region: API gateway -> orchestrator -> model router -> inference gateway -> model server. Each costs hypothetical.streaming_ref.in_region_hop_forward_ms.

stop_at_visible_token.note: Illustrative moment of the Stop press: the 120th visible token of pass 3 of the reference request.

crash_ref._about: Part 17.3 GPU worker crash during pass 3 of the reference request.

crash_at_visible_token.note: Illustrative: the decode worker dies after the client has shown 200 visible tokens of pass 3.

inference_readiness_period_s.note: Readiness probe period on model-server pods (shorter than the Kubernetes default of 10 s so a dead engine leaves the endpoint set faster).

inference_readiness_failure_threshold.note: Failed probes before the pod is not ready (default is 3).

engine_warmup_s.note: Time for a re-formed DEP16 decode worker to start after its weights are in HBM: NCCL and NIXL setup, memory profiling, CUDA Graph capture. Assumption; a real deployment measures it.

region_failover_ref._about: Part 17.4 region failure: detection, traffic shift and the conversation store's cross-region standby (refines RA-17).

global_health_interval_s.note: Interval of the health checks that the PoPs and the global traffic manager run against each region's ingress.

global_health_failures_to_down.note: Consecutive failed checks before global traffic management marks a region down.

weight_push_s.note: Time for the new region weights to reach every PoP proxy (xDS push).

standby_region.note: Region that holds the asynchronous standby of ap_south's home-region data; the same region pair as Part 14's capacity partner (demand_curve:planning.regions.ap_south.partner).

async_replication_lag_s.note: Typical lag of the asynchronous cross-region standby of the conversation store; CockroachDB documents lag for its physical cluster replication 'generally in the tens-of-seconds range' (SRC-687), so 10 s is the low end.

slow_db_ref._about: Part 17.5 slow conversation store: the Part 03 connection-pool example under slowdown.

slowdown_factors.note: Illustrative slowdowns of every transaction (a hot range, a leaseholder move, a long compaction).

db_call_timeout_ms.note: Per-transaction timeout of the orchestrator on the conversation store: 40 times the normal 5 ms, far below the 1 s history-read cap.

retry_ref._about: Part 17.8 retry policy values that RA-12 leaves open.

backoff_base_s.note: Base of the full-jitter exponential backoff.

backoff_cap_s.note: Cap of the backoff; far below the 20 s web_search deadline.

stack_layers.note: Depth of the call stack in the amplification example (edge, gateway, orchestrator, tool executor, provider client), the same five-deep stack as the AWS example.

jitter_seed.note: RNG seed of the sampled sleeps.

queue_burst_ref._about: Part 17.7 queue-collapse example (the note-06 numbers: capacity 100 req/s, arrivals 110 req/s, 10 s client timeout, bound 200).

capacity_rps.note: Service capacity of the toy server: 10 servers, exponential service with mean 0.1 s.

servers.note: Parallel servers of the toy service.

client_timeout_s.note: A client gives up after 10 s without a response; the server does not know.

queue_bound.note: Bounded queue length; an arrival that finds it full gets an immediate 429.

rollout_ref._about: Part 17.10 canary and draining values (RA-54, RA-61).

canary_weights_pct.note: Traffic weights of the new deployment at each canary stage.

canary_stage_hold_s.note: Minimum time at each stage before the next weight, long enough for a few thousand requests at 1%.

drain_timeout_s.note: Bound on active decodes after a worker leaves routing (vLLM --shutdown-timeout); longer than the longest stream at max_tokens 4,096 at 16 tokens/s.

grace_margin_s.note: terminationGracePeriodSeconds = drain_timeout_s + this margin, so Kubernetes never kills a draining engine.

decode_workers_in_pool.note: Size of the ap_south M-frontier decode pool in the example; equals capacity_math:pool.design.decode_workers_needed (Part 09).

max_unavailable_workers.note: Decode workers drained at the same time in one wave.

stream_safety_ref._about: Output moderation on the streamed answer (Part 18.3). What real providers use is not public (class D).

check_window_tokens.note: The orchestrator holds visible text back and sends one output check per 16 new tokens (was 32); a window also closes when a text segment ends (a tool call starts or the message ends). Below NeMo Guardrails' low-latency example (50), above per-token value heads; at 100 tokens/s it holds about a sixth of a second of text.

window_options_tokens.note: Window sizes compared in the hold-back trade-off table (powers of two around the reference choice).

context_overlap_tokens.note: Tokens of the previous window that each check reads again, so a phrase split across two windows is still seen whole. Half the window, the same ratio idea as NeMo's context_size.

check_latency_ms.note: One output check: an in-region gRPC call to the classifier pool plus one batched forward of window + overlap tokens on a 1B-class classifier, including the wait for the next classifier batch. Assumption; a real deployment measures it from traces (RA-52).

classifier_params_reference.note: The output classifier is sized like the public Llama Guard 3 1B model (extra.sims_w18.llama_guard_3_1b_params, SRC-703). Which classifier real providers run is not public.

policy_stop_status.note: A stream that an output check stops is persisted as a partial assistant message with status interrupted (RA-59), holding only the text that was released before the failing window.

policy_stop_reason.note: Reason field stored with the interrupted message and sent in the final error event, so the client can show a policy notice instead of a network error.

log_privacy_ref._about: What the reference request leaves in logs, and how long it stays (Part 18.4).

records_per_component.note: INFO-level records the reference request leaves: one access record at the edge and gateway; orchestrator start, context built, two tool decisions; one per inference pass at the model router; one per tool call; one per fetched page; one VM lifecycle record.

mean_record_bytes.note: Serialized JSON record: timestamp, level, service, trace and span IDs, pseudonymous user ID, tenant ID, request ID, event name, durations, sizes, status. No message text.

debug_sample_fraction.note: Head-sampled share of requests whose DEBUG records are kept (still redacted). Decided once at the edge from the trace ID, so all services keep or drop the same requests.

retention_days.note: Each log class has its own retention and then deletion. Audit events stay just over a year so a yearly review can read the whole year.

pseudonym_key_rotation_days.note: The HMAC key that turns user IDs into log pseudonyms lives in the KMS and rotates every 90 days, so pseudonyms from different quarters cannot be joined without the key.

encryption_ref._about: Encryption at rest and key scopes (Part 18.1, 18.5).

kms_key_scope.value: one key-encryption key per tenant per region
kms_key_scope.note: Every store wraps its data keys with the tenant's regional KMS key, so a key never leaves the tenant's home region and deleting the key makes the tenant's backups unreadable.

data_key_scope.value: one data key per object or per storage range
data_key_scope.note: Envelope encryption (SRC-706): the data key encrypts the bytes, the KMS key encrypts the data key, and the wrapped data key is stored next to the data.

data_key_cache_s.note: How long a service keeps an unwrapped data key in memory before it calls the KMS again; bounds both the KMS request rate and the time a stolen memory image stays useful.

residency_ref._about: Jurisdictions of the reference regions and the two tenants of the residency example (Part 18.5).

region_jurisdiction.note: Each reference region lies in one jurisdiction (RA-05 regions).

reference_tenant_pin.note: The reference user's tenant has no residency contract; its home region ap_south comes from distance.

bound_tenant_pin.note: A second, residency-bound tenant in the example: its contract keeps customer content in India, so only ap_south may hold or process it.

bound_tenant_retry_after_s.note: Retry-After on the 503 that a residency-bound request gets when no allowed region is healthy (fail closed).

observability_ref._about: Service times of the short in-region spans of the reference request's trace, and the telemetry pipeline settings (RA-52). Part 19.1. Longer spans come from earlier data (network_latency, bm25_hnsw_demo, web_search_budget, sandbox_pool, request_cost, capacity_math, sse_framing).

edge_proxy_ms.note: Time the edge PoP proxy spends on one request before it forwards it: decrypt the QUIC packets, parse the HTTP/3 request, run the WAF rules, create the traceparent.

auth_verify_ms.note: API gateway: verify the session token signature with a cached public key and check a local revocation cache; no network call on the common path.

conversation_read_ms.note: Orchestrator reads the conversation row and its three earlier turns from an in-region replica (RA-17); a few index lookups at about 2 ms each (storage_ref.in_region_commit_ms is the write side).

rag_index_search_ms.note: BM25 and HNSW searches run in parallel over the tenant partition with the ACL filter; the slower of the two (Part 05).

rag_chunk_fetch_ms.note: Read the text of the 100 fused candidates from the chunk store for the reranker.

metrics_scrape_interval_s.note: Prometheus scrape interval for engine and EPP /metrics endpoints; equal to the HPA sync period so one sample per HPA evaluation.

trace_baseline_sample_fraction.note: Tail-based sampling at the collector: keep every trace with an error or an SLO miss, plus this fraction of the rest.

span_bytes.note: Mean encoded size of one span (IDs, name, times, about ten attributes) after OTLP protobuf encoding, before compression.

percentile_sample._about: Seeded TTFT sample of one ap_south pool over one hour, for the percentile and histogram demo (Part 19.2) and the latency burn rate (19.3). A mixture: most requests see a short queue, a small share wait behind long prefills.

samples.note: Sample size; large enough that p99 rests on 100 requests.

body_median_s.note: Median TTFT of the common case (queue + prefill of a mostly cached prompt).

slow_fraction.note: Share of requests that wait behind long uncached prefills or a burst.

slow_median_s.note: Median TTFT of the slow share.

incident_error_fractions.note: Two example incidents for the burn-rate alerts: a bad deploy that fails 2% of requests, and a slow leak that fails 0.3%.

cold_start_ref._about: Step times of one M-frontier DEP16 decode worker cold start that no public source measures for this stack (Part 19.4). Measured llm-d values are in extra.sims_w19. Ranges are low (best path) and high (worst normal path).

node_bind_low_s.note: Kubernetes scheduler binds the pods to a free reserved node set in the same rack.

node_bind_high_s.note: No free trays: a powered-down compute tray must boot, pass health checks and join the cluster.

image_bytes.note: Engine container image (vLLM, PyTorch, CUDA libraries, NIXL); weights are not in the image.

image_pull_GBps.note: Effective pull rate from the in-region registry mirror, limited by layer decompression on the node.

process_start_low_s.note: Python imports and API server start with warm page cache.

process_start_high_s.note: Same with a cold page cache.

cuda_init_low_s.note: CUDA context creation on each GPU.

cuda_init_high_s.note: Same, plus GPU health checks at first use.

nccl_setup_low_s.note: Communicators and NIXL memory registration for 16 ranks inside one NVLink domain.

nccl_setup_high_s.note: Same when ranks wait for the slowest rank to finish loading.

gpus_per_tray.note: A GB300 NVL72 compute tray holds 4 GPUs (72 GPUs in 18 trays); the tray's object-store port is shared by its 4 GPUs.

diagnosis_ref._about: Inputs of the third worked bottleneck case in Part 19.6 (a slow tool).

slow_tool_factor.note: The external search provider becomes three times slower for every query and page (a provider-side incident); timeouts unchanged.

image_gen_ref._about: The image branch of this reference system (Part 20.1). The image model has the public shape of FLUX.1 [dev] (extra.sims_w20); which image models real providers run is not public (class D).

image_px.note: Default square output, the size of the FLUX.1 [dev] card example.

steps.note: Equal to the Diffusers FluxPipeline default (extra.sims_w20.flux_pipeline_default_steps); a guidance-distilled model needs no second CFG pass.

cfg_passes_per_step.note: Guidance distillation folds classifier-free guidance into one pass; a model with true CFG runs 2.

gpus_per_worker.note: 12B parameters in BF16 are 24 GB of weights, so one 80 GB H100 holds the model, the VAE and the text encoders.

max_batch_images.note: Images of the same size and step count share one batch; more raises latency linearly because one image already saturates compute.

vae_decode_ms.note: Latent to 1024x1024 RGB decode on the same GPU after the last step.

prompt_check_ms.note: Text classifier on the image prompt after the tool call, before the GPU job (prompt blocking).

output_check_ms.note: Image classifiers on the decoded image before any byte leaves the worker (output blocking).

encode_and_put_ms.note: PNG encode, provenance manifest sign, and PUT to the regional object store.

signed_url_ttl_s.note: Lifetime of the signed GET URL the client receives; the same lifetime as the sandbox artifact URL (hypothetical.sandbox_vm).

ar_pixels_per_token_side.note: Chameleon-style tokenizer: 512 px / 32 tokens per side = 16 px; used for the autoregressive comparison at 1024 px.

voice_ref._about: Latency budget of one spoken turn and barge-in values (Part 20.2). Real providers do not publish their per-stage budgets (class D).

opus_bitrate_kbps.note: Opus voice bitrate inside RFC 6716's 6-510 kbit/s range; wideband speech is clear at this rate.

uplink_jitter_buffer_ms.note: Server-side jitter buffer depth for the microphone stream (two 20 ms packets).

downlink_jitter_buffer_ms.note: Browser playout buffer for the voice stream (three 20 ms packets); mobile networks jitter more on the downlink path.

endpoint_silence_ms.note: Silence after speech that the VAD needs before it ends the user's turn; shorter values cut users off mid-sentence.

asr_finalize_ms.note: Time after the end of turn for the streaming ASR to emit its last words; most of the delay overlaps the endpoint silence.

llm_ttft_ms.note: First text token for a short spoken turn: the system prompt and history hit the prefix cache (RA-40), the new text is a few dozen tokens.

tts_first_phrase_tokens.note: The TTS worker starts after the first phrase so that prosody has a clause to work with.

tts_first_audio_ms.note: Streaming TTS time from the first phrase to the first 20 ms audio frame.

native_turn_detect_ms.note: A semantic turn detector in a native speech model ends the turn earlier than silence alone.

speech_words_per_minute.note: Typical conversational speaking rate of the synthesized voice.

tokens_per_word.note: English text with a BPE tokenizer.

barge_in_min_speech_ms.note: Speech the VAD must hear during playback before it calls a barge-in, so a cough does not stop the answer.

tts_realtime_factor.note: The TTS worker produces 4 s of audio per second of wall time once it runs.

barge_in_at_playback_s.note: Illustrative: the user starts to speak 3 s into the spoken answer.

tts_lookahead_cap_s.note: The voice gateway lets the TTS run at most 2 s of audio ahead of playback, which bounds the audio thrown away on a barge-in.

agent_task_ref._about: One deep-research task as a background job (Part 20.3). Per-pass token sizes reuse hypothetical.workload_profiles (workload C).

passes.note: 39 tool passes and one final report pass; a multi-source research question.

raised_max_passes.note: Loop limit for background research tasks, raised from 8 because a budget now bounds the task.

searches_per_pass.note: Mean queries a tool pass sends; at most 4 calls run in parallel (hypothetical.tool_exec_limits.max_parallel_calls_per_pass).

fetch_wait_s.note: Page fetches after the searches, in parallel, under the 6 s total fetch limit (Part 07).

compaction_trigger_tokens.note: Working context of a task above which the orchestrator runs a compaction pass: the model writes a summary (hypothetical.context_budget_ref.compaction_summary_tokens) of all old tool results, which then replace them. Well under the 131,072-token prompt cap (RA-68).

task_usd_budget.note: Per-task spending cap the orchestrator checks before every pass; the task finishes with what it has when the next pass would exceed it.

wall_clock_limit_s.note: A task that runs longer than one hour stops and writes a partial report.

checkpoint_bytes.note: Plan, step cursor, compacted notes, source list and artifact IDs; tool results themselves live in the object store.

client_disconnect_per_min.note: Chance that one client connection breaks in a given minute (phone sleeps, network change, tab closed).

push_ttl_s.note: TTL header of the Web Push message that says the report is ready.

super_trace_ref._about: Short steps of the reference request that no earlier part timed (Part 21.1).

client_handler_ms.note: From the key press to the request leaving the browser: OS input event to the renderer, the click handler (optimistic render into the store, IDs, JSON), and fetch() handing the request to the network stack on the open HTTP/3 connection (Part 2.1). One short event-loop task.

model_router_ms.note: Model router per pass: evaluate the rule table (RA-56) and run one Redis Lua call for the TPM reservation (RA-10, RA-73) inside the region.

tool_dispatch_ms.note: Orchestrator per tool call: parse the call, validate it against the schema, check the policy (RA-14, RA-65), and append the result to the context. Not counted inside the tool step times of Parts 07 and 08.

async_work_ref._about: Side work after or beside the critical path (Part 21.4). Used only to show what the request would wait for if the work were synchronous.

event_append_ms.note: One acknowledged append to the in-region event log with acks=all and min.insync.replicas 2 (RA-20): one network round trip to the leader plus the follower fetch.

memory_extraction_s.note: Memory worker per turn (RA-27, Part 5.5): one extraction prompt on a small model at low priority, a dedupe search and the record writes.

turn_index_s.note: Conversation indexing per turn: embed the new user message and answer on the retrieval pool's background band and insert the vectors (RA-68).

follow_up_text.value: Redo the chart with Cedar Systems' price 10% lower.
follow_up_text.note: Generic, original follow-up; it needs run_python again on the same files.

price_cut_fraction.note: The price reduction that the follow-up turn asks for (Part 21.6); the same number as in follow_up_text, kept numeric so that text can use a placeholder.

history_keeps.value: user message with its attachments, and the final answer text with its citations
history_keeps.note: What turn 4 becomes in the history of turn 5. The raw reasoning (RA-72) and the tool results stay in the stored message metadata and do not enter later contexts.

latency_tail_ref._about: Tail assumption of the TTFT and latency budget (Part 22.5). Each hop keeps the p50 that an earlier part computed; its time is drawn from a log-normal distribution with that median and the p95/p50 ratio below. No public per-hop tail exists for this hypothetical system.

samples.note: Monte Carlo draws of the whole request; enough for a stable p99 (2,000 draws above it).

seed.note: Fixed seed so the data file is deterministic.

access_p95_over_p50.note: Access network one way (Wi-Fi or mobile radio, home router queues): the most variable network hop. Applied to the user-to-PoP leg in both directions.

backbone_p95_over_p50.note: Backbone one way: the fiber delay is fixed physics; router queues and a longer route on some paths add up to 20 % at p95.

cpu_service_p95_over_p50.note: Short CPU services (browser handler, edge checks, gateway, context assembly, model router, tool dispatch, final write): garbage-collection pauses, CPU contention and cold caches triple a few-ms step at p95.

retrieval_p95_over_p50.note: Retrieval fan-out (embedding, index search, chunk fetch, rerank on the retrieval GPU pool): the reranker batch wait and the slowest index shard double it at p95.

queue_p95_over_p50.note: Gateway queue plus engine wait per pass. An exponential waiting time has p95/p50 = ln 20 / ln 2 = 4.3; 4.0 keeps the same order without claiming an exact M/M/c shape.

gpu_work_p95_over_p50.note: Vision encoder, prefill and the KV transfer of one pass: the token count is fixed, but other prompts share the token budget of each step (chunked prefill), so the time stretches by up to 50 % at p95.

sandbox_p95_over_p50.note: run_python tool step: the code run and the artifact upload on a shared sandbox host.

cost_model_ref._about: Unit prices of the non-GPU cost centers (Part 22.6). Round numbers of the same order as public cloud list prices; not any provider's cost and not any company's economics. GPU-hour prices come from hypothetical.fleet_price_ref (Part 12).

vcpu_hour_usd.note: CPU tier (edge, gateway, orchestrator, model router, search engine) and sandbox hosts; one price for every general-purpose vCPU.

cpu_us_per_event_per_hop.unit: µs per SSE event per forwarding hop
cpu_us_per_event_per_hop.note: CPU time of one forwarder for one stream event: read, frame, write, flow-control bookkeeping (RA-47, RA-74).

db_usd_per_million_writes.note: Distributed SQL write with quorum replication inside the home region (RA-17); the price covers the replicas.

db_usd_per_million_reads.note: Distributed SQL read served by one replica (RA-17).

db_storage_usd_per_gb_month.note: Conversation store storage, per logical GB per replica.

object_storage_usd_per_gb_month.note: S3-class object store for uploaded files (RA-21).

internet_egress_usd_per_gb.note: Bytes from the edge to the user's browser (the SSE stream).

cross_region_usd_per_gb.note: Bytes between two regions, for example the asynchronous standby copy of the conversation store (RA-79).

telemetry_usd_per_gb.note: Traces, structured logs and analytics events ingested by the telemetry pipeline (RA-52, RA-77, RA-20); retention priced in.

storage_months_counted.note: The per-request cost counts one month of storage for the files and message rows a request creates; longer retention scales these two lines linearly.

utilization_points.note: GPU utilization points of the sensitivity table; the fleet's daily utilization from Part 14.8 is added from data.

overload_burst_ref._about: Paper simulation of an overload burst (Part 22.8, R-XXII.8): a toy pool of identical serving units, FIFO queue, Poisson arrivals, exponential service. Each unit stands for one 8-GPU unit of an M-frontier rack; the warm spare is the rack's 9th 8-GPU unit (RA-55).

servers.note: The 64 active GPUs of one RA-55 rack counted in 8-GPU units.

capacity_rps.note: Total service rate of the 8 units, the same 100 requests/s as the toy service of Part 17.7, so mean service = 8 / 100 = 80 ms.

base_arrival_rps.note: Arrival rate before and after the burst: utilization 0.7, below the autoscaling target.

burst_arrival_rps.note: Arrival rate during the burst: 10 % above capacity, the same overload as Part 17.7.

burst_start_s.note: Start of the burst after the simulation starts.

burst_duration_s.note: A three-minute burst, for example a news event (Part 14.7).

duration_s.note: Simulated time; long enough for every scenario to drain.

warm_spare_servers.note: RA-55 keeps 8 warm-spare GPUs per 64 active GPUs: one more 8-GPU unit, 12.5 % more capacity, weights already loaded.

warm_spare_join_s.note: From the scale-up decision until the spare takes traffic: one readiness-probe period (RA-51), no weight load and no CUDA initialization.

autoscale_target_utilization.note: KEDA scales the pool so that the measured arrival rate uses at most 80 % of capacity (RA-42); the same bound as the batch band ceiling of Part 9.4.

seed.note: Fixed seed for the arrival and service draws.
